articles.title: Tim Cook's parting message: Apple is in the hands of a product builder | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Tim Cook’s farewell memo to Apple employees offers a glimpse at how he wants John Ternus to be seen: as a product builder with deep experience across the iPhone, Mac, AirPods, and other major hardware lines.
articles.body:
On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook offered a rousing endorsement of his successor: John Ternus , the company’s senior vice president of hardware engineering. In a memo to employees, Cook reminded staff that he’s “not leaving Apple,” just stepping away from the role of CEO, while declaring that “few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does.”

Ternus’ elevation to the top job suggests that Apple’s next era will see a renewed focus on hardware and product execution. Under Ternus, Apple shipped a number of notable products, most recently, the new ultra-thin iPhone Air, the lower-cost MacBook Neo, and AirPods with hearing health features. He also led the hardware engineering team across Apple’s full device lineup.

Hardware will play an important role in the AI era, not only in terms of chips, but also the devices people use to run enterprise AI. Apple this year, for instance, offered earlier releases of its new Mac models, the Mac mini and Mac Studio, compared with years past, driven by AI demand.

Cook’s memo, reported by Bloomberg and others, naturally says little about Apple’s future when it comes to AI, services, regulation, China, or the other challenges that lie ahead. Instead, Cook focuses on his gratitude for the opportunity to lead Apple and exalts the company’s culture as ultimately what matters most.

“We share a belief that what we build matters and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it,” Cook wrote. He also referenced the famous Steve Jobs quote about leaving a “dent in the universe,” saying that Apple makes that possible because of “who we are and what we believe,” as well as “what we value and how we see the world.”

Cook will remain at Apple as executive chairman and will continue to manage political relationships, including those with President Trump and the Chinese government.

On X, Cook also wrote : “Sending lots of love to the Apple community on my last day as CEO. My title changes tomorrow, but the love I have for the Apple community never will. Thank you for being a constant source of inspiration. My gratitude is endless, and I’m excited for the next chapter!”

articles.title: Car owners want tech they can ignore
articles.summary: Car owners don’t mind more tech in their vehicles, as long as its easy to ignore, according to a new survey from JD Power.
articles.body: Automakers keep shoving more tech into their cars, despite evidence that consumers are increasingly fed up with huge screens and glitchy software. In fact, the features that car owners appreciate the most happen to be the ones they barely notice, according to the latest tech survey from JD Power. The consumer research firm surveyed 68,084 owners of new 2026 model-year vehicles after 90 days of ownership. The survey touched on 40 automotive technologies covering comfort and convenience; connected vehicles; driver assist; electric vehicles; and smart vehicles. The features that scored the highest were the ones that were the most inconspicuous, like smart ignition, in which the vehicle automatically starts and turns off based on driver actions, or smart HVAC systems, which use AI to automatically adjust the cabin environment for maximum comfort and efficiency. These were the big winners in JD’s survey — mostly because they require the least attention from the driver. Smart ignition, in particular, delivered the highest overall satisfaction, with only 2.4 problems per 100 vehicles. “For automakers, the opportunity is to prioritize technology that makes driving simpler, not more complicated,” Doron Hikry, director of customer success at JD Power, said in a press release. “The features that solve real problems without adding effort or stress for the driver are the ones resonating most with customers.” Superfluous tech features like passenger screens, in which an extra screen is embedded in the dash in front of passengers, rated the lowest in satisfaction. These screens first began cropping up in premium brands, like Mercedes, BMW, and Porsche, but have yet to bleed over to more mass-market vehicles. Apparently, they’re just wasted space on the dash, with more than one-third of owners who have a passenger screen reporting they’ve never tried to use it. Only 6 percent admitted to using their passenger screens every time they drive. Yikes. Another tech feature that has more work to do in winning over customers is hands-free driving, also known as Level 2 Plus automation. These are features like Tesla’s Full Self-Driving, Ford’s BlueCruise, GM’s Super Cruise, and Mercedes’ Drive Pilot. Unlike Level 2 systems, which require drivers to keep their hands on the steering wheel, these L2 Plus systems allow for completely hands-free driving on certain roads. Car owners told JD Power they preferred L2 systems in terms of design and quality of experience, suggesting that more automation does not necessarily mean more customer satisfaction. Interestingly, Level 2 systems were recording slightly higher problems per 100 vehicles (14.3) as L2 Plus ones (13.8). “The results indicate that owners may currently be more comfortable with systems that clearly assist the driver rather than those that introduce a greater degree of automation,” said Hikry. What these results suggest is that car owners don’t necessarily mind more technology in their vehicles, just as long as they don’t make the task of driving more complicated. The individual awards underscore this point: The Cadillac Escalade and Toyota Tundra both won for camera mirrors, while other automakers notched wins for blind-spot cameras, digital keys, one-pedal driving, and EV charging schedulers.

articles.title: JMGO’s very bright all-in-one projector looks ideal for gamers and sports
articles.summary: The Iris Ultra Max brings 4K, 120Hz, VRR, ALLM, 6500 ISO lumens, and dual-iris contrast control.
articles.body: JMGO’s 4K 120Hz Iris Ultra Max all-in-one Google TV projector is now available outside China. It gets its name from a new dual-iris system that lets it produce an impressive 10,000:1 native contrast, according to JMGO. It boosts the contrast — always an issue with projectors — by placing two separate physical apertures (irises) along different points of the internal optical path to control light scatter and brightness far more aggressively than a single iris can. It also promises to produce a very bright 6,500 ISO lumen image from its triple-laser light engine. Last year at IFA, 6,000 lumens from an all-in-one projector was breaking new ground. At IFA 2026, it’s shaping up to be table stakes, alongside 4k imagery purring along at a smooth 120Hz for fast-moving sports and gaming. Just note that I found JMGO’s N3 Ultimate to be unwatchable at peak brightness due to color distortion — so best wait for the reviews on this one. Like that previous flagship, the new Iris Ultra Max is mounted on a motorized pan-and-tilt gimbal for useful Wiimote-like control. That, combined with an 0.88–1.7:1 optical zoom and V±130% / H±53% lens shift, gives you unparalleled image placement options that also preserve optical image quality. [Image: A look around back. JGMO’s also tossing in VRR and ALLM to keep latency low and reduce tearing when gaming on the IRIS Ultra Max, with support for Dolby Vision HDR at 4K 120Hz. It will eventually list for $3,499, but that drops to $2,999 for preorders that begin today, ahead of an October 19th ship date.

articles.title: Free flow: golpes já somam 480 sites falsos que cobram pedágio | G1
articles.standfirst: Criminosos criam sites que pedem diretamente a placa do veículo e, em seguida, oferecem um suposto pagamento pelas passagens no sistema de pedágio eletrônico.
articles.summary: Criminosos criam sites que pedem diretamente a placa do veículo e, em seguida, oferecem um suposto pagamento pelas passagens no sistema de pedágio eletrônico.
articles.body:
Pórtico do Free Flow no Rio Grande do Sul — Foto: Gustavo Mansur/Palácio Piratini

Em um ano, o número de sites falsos que prometem regularizar passagens pelo sistema "free flow" chegou a 480, segundo levantamento da Kaspersky.

🔎 O free flow é um sistema de pedágio eletrônico sem cancelas que permite cobrar a tarifa sem que o motorista precise parar ou reduzir a velocidade.

Em apenas uma semana, foram criados 80 sites que supostamente identificam a passagem por pórticos do free flow e geram uma falsa cobrança por PIX.

Segundo o estudo, os sites falsos vão direto ao assunto:

Há pouco texto que permita perceber que a página não pertence à concessionária responsável pelo trecho onde o motorista passou;

Em destaque, uma caixa de texto pede a placa do veículo;

Em seguida, o valor é exibido junto com o PIX para pagamento.

O estudo identificou casos em que a cobrança era de cerca de R$ 25.

O valor baixo ajuda a reduzir a desconfiança dos motoristas e a imitar tarifas reais de pedágio. Na BR-101, por exemplo, a passagem de carros de passeio pelo trecho entre Paraty (RJ) e Rio de Janeiro (RJ) pode custar R$ 4,80.

“Ao acreditar na legitimidade da cobrança, o usuário paga via PIX, e o dinheiro é transferido para contas de ‘laranjas’”, diz o estudo.

Aplicativo da CNH resolve parte do problema

Na semana passada, o Ministério dos Transportes atualizou o aplicativo CNH do Brasil. Com a mudança, os motoristas passaram a consultar na plataforma as passagens registradas em pedágios do sistema free flow .

No aplicativo, que já reunia informações da Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) e sobre multas, o motorista pode consultar as passagens por pedágios eletrônicos em rodovias municipais, estaduais e federais, independentemente da concessionária.

Além de informar quando o veículo passou pelo pórtico, o app CNH do Brasil mostra onde e como pagar a tarifa.

Antes da nova funcionalidade, o motorista precisava acessar os canais de atendimento de cada concessionária para consultar e pagar as tarifas. A falta de um sistema centralizado dificultava os pagamentos e abria espaço para golpes com sites falsos.

O estudo da Kaspersky destaca os benefícios de concentrar as informações em um só lugar.

Porém, mesmo com a novidade, ainda são identificados "novos sites falsos que simulam cobranças do free flow. Os cibercriminosos acompanham os assuntos em destaque no noticiário e nas redes sociais para adaptar rapidamente suas estratégias, e fica o alerta para possíveis novas iscas relacionadas ao tema nos próximos meses”, diz Fabio Assolini, pesquisador da Kaspersky.

O estudo não identificou um número expressivo de aplicativos que se passam pelo CNH do Brasil, mas apontou que já existem apps para Android e iPhone com nomes muito parecidos com o oficial.

Consulte o free flow apenas pelo aplicativo oficial CNH Digital , disponível para Android e iPhone ;

Se você utiliza uma tag de pagamento, a cobrança é feita pelo sistema já adotado pela operadora , como fatura mensal ou pagamento antecipado;

Não clique em alertas de passagens enviados por mensagem nem em anúncios exibidos em buscadores;

Fique atento ao destinatário do PIX: o valor do pedágio não deve ser pago a pessoas físicas nem a fintechs.

articles.title: Government sounds alarm, ads on Facebook ‌and Instagram found directing users to apps that steal banking passwords and remotely control users' phones
articles.summary: Tech News News: The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. In an advisory, National Cybe.
articles.body: The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. In an advisory, National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) said that it has observed a rise in financial frauds perpetrated through malicious Android apps masquerading as pornography apps, circulated through Facebook and Instagram ads. As per the Ministry of Home Affairs advisory, these Android apps are operating under the names "Night Play", "Reloop", "Kyss", “Vimo”, “Rivo”, “Nexo”, “Vixa” and other similar variants.These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content, where the user is prompted to download an APK file. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional apps and by misusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device. Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route internet traffic pertaining to malicious/criminal activity. As per government warning, these apps can secretly access information stored on users' phones, capture one-time passwords and bank PINs, and transfer money from ​accounts without the owner's knowledge. Not just this, the apps also make it difficult for users to uninstall them through device's normal settings.How these apps work, spy and stealDistribution: The malicious apps are distributed through pornographic content related advertisements or links majorly on Facebook and Instagram. These ads redirect to phishing websites.Redirection: Ads redirect to phishing websites serving pornographic content. Domains of the website majorly belong to “.live”. Users are persuaded to download and install the APK from sources outside the Google Play Store.App Update: A secondary package gets downloaded and installed on the pretext of an app update, based on permissions abused by the first, initial app.Abuse of Accessibility Permission for device takeover: After installation, the app asks users to grant Accessibility and other sensitive permissions. Once enabled, the malware gains control of the device and continues to run in the background.VPN Installation: Some apps may also install a VPN on the device, thereby routing all internet traffic through attacker-controlled servers. This compromises user's transmitted data, which may subsequently be exploited for malicious or criminal activities.Unauthorized Transactions: Since the malware has the ability to take over the compromised device, installing such apps may lead to financial fraud.How to uninstall these appsMETHOD 1: Safe Mode RebootStep 1: Start Your Phone in Safe Mode: Press and hold the Power button. Press and hold Power Off until the Safe Mode option appears. Click OK or Restart in Safe Mode. Wait for the phone to restart. "Safe Mode" will appear at the bottom of the screen.Step 2: Uninstall the App: Open Settings. Go to Apps. Select the suspicious application. Tap Uninstall. Remove any other unknown or related apps.Step 3: Restart Normally: Restart the phone. The device will exit Safe Mode automatically.Second MethodStep 1: Restore the Default Home Screen (If required): Open Settings. Go to Apps → Default Apps → Home App. Select your phone's original launcher (System Launcher, One UI Home, Pixel Launcher, etc.).Step 2: Disable Accessibility Access: Open Settings. Tap Accessibility. Open Installed Services or Downloaded Apps. Select the suspicious application. Turn Accessibility Off.Step 3: Remove Administrator Access: Open Settings. Go to Security or Security & Privacy.Open Device Admin Apps or Device Administrators. If the suspicious app is enabled, select it. Tap Deactivate or Turn Off.Verify the Device: Open Settings > Apps. Confirm that the suspicious application has been removed. If the app cannot be removed or returns after restarting, back up your important data and perform a Factory Reset.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: As Apple gets new CEO, Fortnite-maker Epic Games CEO, who has been in court battle with the iPhone maker since years, has a message: "I hope Apple looks…
articles.summary: Tech News News: John Ternus formally took charge as Apple's chief executive on September 1, and one of the first public messages addressed to the new boss came from t.
articles.body: John Ternus formally took charge as Apple's chief executive on September 1, and one of the first public messages addressed to the new boss came from the man who has spent six years suing his company. Tim Sweeney, the Epic Games founder behind Fortnite, posted in the early hours of Tuesday that Apple was entering a new age, and that the eras in the company's history have been read very differently by users, developers and shareholders.The timing was deliberate. Tim Cook spent his last day as CEO on August 31 sending a farewell memo to staff and stays on as executive chairman, handling policymakers and government relationships. Sweeney used the handover to make a direct pitch to the incoming CEO, an engineer who ran Apple's hardware group and shipped the iPhone Air, the MacBook Neo and the hearing-aid AirPods before moving into the top job.Sweeney wants Apple to grow the pie instead of taking a bigger slice of itHis longer post reads less like a legal position and more like an appeal to what Apple used to be. Here it is in full:"I hope Apple looks toward the future as optimistically as I do, seeing a blue ocean of opportunity to radically advance the hardware, the intelligence of the software, and the quality and spirit of the whole app ecosystem for everyone's benefit. A company that looks to grow its business by bringing computing more meaningfully to everyone's lives and by creating more value from its own efforts, rather than extracting ever more from a world on fire. I grew up in the era of the Apple of Woz, profoundly influenced by a computer empowering anyone to boot up, write programs, and share them with others. I believe that's the ideal all developers should hold out for, and that the necessities of privacy and security are absolutely compatible with robust competition among stores, payments, and the other things. Let the best win."The Epic vs Apple fight started with a payment button inside Fortnite in 2020Epic sued Apple and Google in August 2020 after adding a direct payment option to Fortnite, which got the game pulled from both app stores. Sweeney has said the legal bills in the Apple case alone crossed $100 million, and that Fortnite had earned roughly $300 million on iOS in its two years there. Counting lost players and the network effect of friends who could not join, he has put the total damage to Epic at a billion dollars or more.Apple now wants settlement talks, and Epic is not in a hurry to take themThe fight is still live. In mid-August, Apple asked a federal court in California to push both sides into a supervised settlement conference, days after Epic turned down a direct approach. Apple simultaneously proposed a new fee structure for purchases made through outside payment links, ranging from 15 percent on standard apps down to 5 percent for small developers. Epic called those fees far outside the appeals court's guidance and said it has about 60 days to file its opposition.Ternus inherits all of it, along with a September 9 event and a company worth about $4.6 trillion. Whether his Apple is a different Apple for developers will be settled in a courtroom, not in a memo.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: John Ternus is now the CEO of Apple
articles.summary: Apple’s CEO transition has handed leadership over from Tim Cook to John Ternus, ahead of its iPhone launch event scheduled for September 9th.
articles.body: For the first time since 2011, one of the world’s most valuable companies has a new leader, as today marks John Ternus’ first day as Apple’s CEO. He’s replacing Tim Cook, who will continue on as the executive chairman on Apple’s board and departed with a letter to employees that remarked, “This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters, and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it.” Ternus is taking over a company dealing with the rise of AI, shortages of RAM and other components due to that growth in AI, and a political and economic situation that is only getting more complicated as time passes. He will also do it without many of the executives who worked with Cook and Steve Jobs, like Phil Schiller, who Bloomberg reported will step down from his role leading the App Store. Here’s a look at Apple’s senior leadership team as it stands today: [Image: Here’s what Apple’s leadership team looked like under Tim Cook, and what it now looks like under John Ternus. With Ternus in charge, Tim Cook has been moved to Executive Chair and Phil Schiller continues as an Apple Fellow, despite handing off his day-to-day tasks of heading up the Apple Store and Apple events. We can also see that Katherine Adams’ position of SVP of government affairs has been fully vacated, with some of that responsibility being handed to Jennifer Newstead and Tim Cook, who’s now Trump’s full-time handler. Apple’s former CFO Luca Maestri is no longer listed on the leadership team after he transitioned to the roll of VP of corporate services in 2024. The first Apple hardware event of the Ternus era is just around the corner on September 9th, where we expect to see new iPhones including a foldable “Ultra.” It will give us an early glimpse of what to expect, and the new public faces of the company going forward.

articles.title: TP-Link’s first Wi-Fi 8 router is almost here
articles.summary: TP-Link unveiled the Archer 8 Ultra router and Deco 8 Ultra mesh system, which will use Wi-Fi 8 to “address the connectivity problems people actually notice.”
articles.body: The Wi-Fi 8 standard is far from finalized, but TP-Link is almost ready to release its first hardware targeting the next-gen spec. It unveiled the Archer 8 Ultra tri-band router and Deco 8 Ultra mesh system at IFA 2026, which utilize the upcoming IEEE 802.11bn standard to “address the connectivity problems people actually notice” instead of focusing on speed upgrades, according to TP-Link’s announcement. The Archer 8 Ultra features 18 internal antennas, and can deliver wireless speeds of up to 19Gbps and 10Gbps over wired connection. The Deco 8 Ultra mesh system provides up to 22Gbps over wireless and 10Gbps wired connectivity, according to TP-Link, with a three-pack covering up to 9,800 square feet and supporting more than 200 connected devices. TP-Link hasn’t revealed any prices, but says the Archer 8 Ultra will be available for preorder in “select regions” starting on September 30th. Availability for the Deco 8 is planned for sometime in Q1 2027, with other Wi-Fi 8 products — including range extenders, adapters, and the Roam 8 travel router — to follow in Q2 2027. The Wi-Fi 7 standard was only finalized in January 2024, so these new products are set to arrive before many people have had the chance to upgrade to the previous specification. Wi-Fi 8 also isn’t expected to receive a finalized certification until May 2028. TP-Link clearly wants to get ahead of the competition, however, and soothe any concerns regarding how its next-gen products will be impacted by the US ban on foreign-made routers — while TP-Link’s Wi-Fi 8 products use Broadcom, Qualcomm, and MediaTek chipsets, it says it’s using “US-led hardware and software engineering to deliver the most reliable Wi-Fi ever built.”

articles.title: Tim Cook’s Apple: his 10 biggest wins and misses
articles.summary: Tim Cook is officially out as CEO at Apple after a 15-year tenure that came with plenty of wins and misses.
articles.body: Expectations for Tim Cook were almost impossibly high when he stepped in to replace Apple’s visionary cofounder in 2011. He inherited a company on a blockbuster run, after Steve Jobs returned and revitalized the Mac, launched the iPod, and oversaw the launch of the iPhone. Now, after 15 years in the CEO role, Tim Cook is stepping down. He’s replaced today by hardware leader John Ternus. Over the course of Cook’s tenure, Apple accomplished a lot, with the launch of plenty of new products, features, and services that the company just wouldn’t be the same without. There were plenty of ups and downs, but Cook helped cement the company as one of the most profitable tech companies on the planet. Here’s a look back at Cook’s legacy — including his biggest wins at the company and his biggest misses. Win: Growing Apple’s services business When Cook became CEO, he had a strange problem: The iPhone was so successful that it made up half of Apple’s revenue, and he needed to diversify. To do this, Cook turned to Apple’s services business, which began ramping up with the launch of the App Store in 2008. Under Cook, it has grown into a massive source of revenue for the company, topped only by sales from the iPhone. Though Steve Jobs originally announced iCloud in June 2011, Cook oversaw its launch after taking over as CEO just months later. Apple’s services business continued to grow since then, with Cook launching Apple Pay in 2014, followed by Apple Music in 2015. The company later revealed a flurry of new services in 2019: Apple TV, Apple Arcade, Apple News Plus, and its own credit card. It even debuted its own Fitness Plus workout subscription, along with an Apple One plan that bundles all of its services together. Last year, Apple reported earning $100 billion from all of its services combined. Win: Apple silicon [Image: While at the helm, Cook led an initiative to transition Macs away from Intel chips and onto Apple’s own custom processors. The transition could have been a disaster: The hardware could have been weaker, the software could have suffered from years of sluggish work from developers — both realities experienced when the Windows world tried to make a similar transition to Arm-based chips. Instead, Apple began the switch in 2020 after revealing its own ARM-based chip, the M1, which exceeded expectations following its debut in the MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, and the Mac mini. The chips have continued to give Apple a performance edge and free it from the sometimes rocky Intel development cycle. Since then, Apple has released six generations of its M-series chips, with the most recent M6 being the company’s first built on the more efficient 2-nanometer process. Apple officially finished its switch away from Intel in 2023. Aside from its in-house Mac chips, Apple also launched its first 5G modem in the iPhone 16E under Cook. Win: Apple’s foray into wearables and health [Image: In the years after Cook became CEO, Apple expanded its product lineup beyond the iPhone, Mac, and iPod. Cook led the launch of the Apple Watch in 2015, which has gone from a companion device for the iPhone to an advanced health-tracking wearable with the ability to take ECGs, flag irregular heartbeats, and detect sleep apnea. Apple also became one of the first major tech companies to launch wireless earbuds with the release of the AirPods in 2016. The company even managed to incorporate health-focused capabilities into its earbuds, as it introduced an FDA-authorized hearing aid feature with the AirPods Pro 2 and added built-in hearing protection. Cook himself acknowledged Apple’s impact on user health, saying during a 2019 interview: “...If you zoom out into the future, and you look back, and you ask the question, ‘What was Apple’s greatest contribution to mankind?’ it will be about health.” Win: Making Apple the first US company to hit a $1 trillion market cap In 2011, Apple was ascendant, riding high on the first few generations of the iPhone. Cook took the reins and capitalized on the momentum, transforming the company into a market-dominating powerhouse. In 2018, Apple became the first US company to reach a market capitalization of more than $1 trillion. The company has since hit $2 trillion, $3 trillion, and $4 trillion market cap milestones, as Cook’s leadership and command of the supply chain propelled the company to higher profits. Win: Fighting for user privacy Apple made headlines in 2015 after refusing to build a backdoor into the iPhone 5C belonging to one of the shooters in the San Bernardino terrorist attack on privacy grounds. At the time, Cook published a letter to customers, saying the government’s request is an “unprecedented step which threatens the security of our customers” and would have “implications far beyond the legal case at hand.” The company is now in a similar fight in the UK, where it’s pushing back on demands to build a backdoor into encrypted iCloud user data, and recently filed another legal challenge against the request. Aside from these fights, Apple has introduced a number of privacy-focused features under Cook, including Private Relay and Advanced Data Protection, and a Private Cloud Compute system to protect AI queries. Miss: Vision Pro [Image: Though Cook may have been successful in introducing Apple into the wearables space, the same can’t be said for the company’s entry into virtual reality. The Apple Vision Pro launched in 2024 and aimed to change the way you interact with tech by putting apps on your face. But the $3,499 price tag and limited use cases didn’t set it up for mainstream adoption. The Financial Times reported in December 2025 that Apple cut Vision Pro production and marketing due to “weak sales.” Apple also laid off staff who worked on the Vision Pro, while “largely shutting down” a team dedicated to gaming on the headset, according to Bloomberg. Miss: The Apple Car that never was For years, Apple remained tight-lipped about Project Titan, its long-rumored initiative to build a self-driving vehicle. Reports suggest Apple had been working on an autonomous car since at least 2014, as the company continued to drop hints about the project. Cook said in 2017 that Apple is “focusing on autonomous systems,” adding that “clearly, one purpose of autonomous systems are self-driving cars.” This never panned out. After spending more than $10 billion on Project Titan, Apple officially scrapped the idea and disbanded the 2,000-person team behind the project, Bloomberg reported at the time. Miss: Siri and Apple Intelligence struggles [Image: Shortly after taking over as CEO, Cook introduced Siri. In time, its limited capabilities began to lag behind rival voice assistants, often struggling to answer simple questions. Apple outfitted Siri with a more natural-sounding voice and made other improvements over the years but never quite delivered on the original promise. Apple’s plan to upgrade Siri with AI was supposed to mark the assistant’s transformation into something actually useful — except it didn’t go as planned. Apple initially took the wraps off a more conversational Siri in June 2024, but later delayed its launch, saying in March 2025 that it’s “going to take us longer than we thought” to deliver promised features, like the ability for Siri to control apps on your behalf. The development drama didn’t end there, as Apple replaced AI chief John Giannandrea and agreed to pay $250 million for allegedly misleading customers about AI Siri. The AI-upgraded Siri, powered by a custom version of Google Gemini, is now on track to launch this fall — more than two years after it was announced. Miss: App Store monopoly mishaps In 2020, Epic Games sued Apple after the iPhone maker removed Fortnite from the App Store for directing users to Epic’s own payment processor. The lengthy legal battle that ensued shone a light on the lengths a Cook-controlled Apple would go to keep its control over the App Store — and the commission it earns from in-app purchases. App store regulations in the European Union only amplified this, as Apple introduced a convoluted carveout for developers wanting to distribute apps on alternative app stores. The company says it has since “resolved” a disagreement with the EU over its policies, but the struggle to get it to comply speaks to just how much Apple has come to rely on App Store revenue. And while Apple may not mind tussling with regulators, the strict policies have for years frustrated developers on its platform — an audience that’s important to Apple’s success. Miss: The rocky release of Apple Maps Apple Maps was a buggy mess following its launch in 2012. As The Verge reported at the time, map details were missing across the US, while other cities like London, Beijing, and Tokyo were “virtually blank” and major landmarks “labeled inaccurately or wildly misplaced.” Cook issued a public apology as the company worked to fix issues across the app. Eddy Cue, Apple’s head of services, said in 2016 that the disastrous launch of Maps led to the company’s decision to test updates in a public beta first. This launch may have been a disaster, but the turnaround has been one of the successes of Cook’s tenure and speaks to his ability to operate the company so effectively. Apple Maps has slowly and steadily improved to the point where it’s now a great component of the iPhone. What Cook’s still on the hook for: Managing Trump [Image: The engraved Corning glass with a 24-karat base that Apple gifted to Trump. Apple’s relationship with President Donald Trump has both helped and hurt the company. Currying favor with the Trump administration has helped Apple avoid steep tariffs, but it’s also appeared at odds with the company’s values on diversity, racial equity, and the environment — and it’s regularly required “Tim Apple” to put himself in embarrassing positions for the sake of the company’s bottom line During Trump’s first term, Cook showed the president around a factory that the president incorrectly took credit for opening. During Trump’s second term, Cook gifted the president an engraved piece of Corning glass with a 24-karat gold base. As executive chairman, Cook will still be on tap to handle Apple’s relationship with Trump.

articles.title: IFA 2026: the biggest tech and gadget announcements
articles.summary: IFA runs from September 4th to 8th, and The Verge will be on the ground in Berlin to bring you all the biggest announcements and hardware hands-ons.
articles.body: Every year over 200,000 people descend on Berlin for IFA, the largest tech trade show in Europe. Some of the world’s biggest manufacturers turn up to demo everything from appliances to smartphones to smart home gadgets, and this year should be no different. IFA itself runs from September 4th to 8th, but most of the biggest news arrives in the day or two before the show officially opens to the public, so keep your eyes peeled for news as it breaks. The Verge will be on the ground in Berlin to see the biggest hardware launches in person and put them through their paces, and we’ll be collecting all the news, announcements, and hands-on demos and videos right here.

articles.title: JBL takes on Sonos with new multi-room Cove speakers
articles.summary: JBL is stepping into the world of connected whole-home audio, with its new Cove series speakers.
articles.body: JBL is well known for its portable bluetooth and party speakers, but now it’s also stepping into the world of connected whole-home audio. The JBL Cove series of speakers introduced today can work independently, as a stereo pair, or linked together to form a multi-room sound system, placing the range in competition with Sonos and Bose’s new Lifestyle Ultra speakers. There are three models in the JBL Cove series, which come in a choice of black or white color options and will be available starting September 13th. There’s the compact $229.95 Cove M1, which includes three 0.75-inch tweeters and a single 4-inch woofer, but requires a wired power source. The larger $399.95 Cove P1 has Dolby Atmos support and the added convenience of being battery-powered, with up to 14 hours of playtime, according to JBL. The $449.95 Cove X1 is the flagship model, which also needs to be plugged into a power outlet, but features four 1.25-inch tweeters and dual 4-inch woofers alongside Dolby Atmos support. The Cove speakers connect together through Wi-Fi and can be managed through the JBL One app for controlling music streams and room groupings. Notable features include automatic self-tuning, JBL’s “AI Sound Boost” technology to prevent audio distortion at high volumes, and a “Music Follows Me” feature that transfers audio to the room you’re in without resorting to a phone, by long-pressing the Moment button on the closest speaker. [Image: In order from left to right, here’s what the JBL Cove M1, Cove X1, and Cove P1 speakers look like in white. Supported services include Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect, AirPlay 2, Google Cast, and Roon Ready. US Alexa Plus subscribers can also access the Amazon assistant through Cove speakers, including voice-activated smart home controls. Each speaker also supports Bluetooth for a direct connection with phones and tablets, and can connect with JBL’s Bar Series MK2 soundbars for an expanded home theater experience.

articles.title: A day-one briefing for Apple’s new CEO
articles.summary: An executive summary to get John Ternus up to speed.
articles.body: Executive Summary, Day One 📁 Inbox 5:05AM To: Ternus, John <jternus@apple.com> Reply-to: CEO-transition-team@apple.com Welcome to your first day as CEO! Hopefully you’re finding your new office spacious and comfortable. If you have trouble with any of the doors just ping us — being a Jony Ive design, you won’t find anything as unsightly as a door handle here! Today’s memo includes a summary of the business, broken out by division. The day’s schedule is also attached; please note that the Apple Intelligence team needed to delay the new Siri discussion until a later date, but they promise they’re “for real” this time. Hardware Everything is in hand for the upcoming phone launches. We don’t anticipate the price hikes will have much impact on sales, since nobody in the US knows how much they really pay for their phone anyway. The team agrees that calling the camera on the upcoming AirPods a “sensor” would make it less creepy and is moving forward with that terminology. Morale on the Vision Pro team after their move to the basement is somewhat low, but we’ve scheduled a virtual offsite for them in Tahiti that we think will help. Services Our new EU app store rules go into effect in exactly one month. We’ve compiled a simplified explainer breaking down how much commission app developers will pay and which companies can operate alternative app stores into an easy-to-parse, 300-page PDF (see attached). This does mean that our services revenue will take a hit, but on the bright side, we just rolled out ads in Maps to juice the numbers. Despite the setbacks, services is still our best bet for growth since we, well, ran out of people to sell iPhones to. It might even become a bigger business than the iPhone someday. That could fundamentally change the kind of company Apple is — a hardware guy in charge of a services company? Or will a services company pivot back to hardware under a new CEO? Striking that balance without frustrating customers remains an ongoing challenge. Take a hint from your predecessor: Ted Lasso is so lovable nobody noticed that we raised Apple TV prices again. Software The good news is that the updated Liquid Glass design is polling with higher approval ratings than last year. The bad news is that Brussels is still mad at us for holding back new Siri in Europe, Google’s kind of eating our lunch in the EU, and app developers are still unhappy with the new commission structure. We were, uh, not winning any popularity contests with app developers to start with, so this may be something to consider. Operation Smarter Siri Take Two has been a success, and we’re finally back in the AI game. Unfortunately, in the time that passed since Smarter Siri The First Try, AI became deeply unfashionable. But it kind of works in our favor; we can let Meta and Google take the heat on building out all those data centers (pun intended?) while we cajole app developers into using app intents so Siri can actually do stuff. Once again, see above point about developers. Side note: Alan Dye was seen near campus holding a sign that reads “Liquid Glass is good, actually” but security handled it. Special Projects The car lab has transitioned nicely into the new AI wearable testing / smart home facility. There’s a little conflict between the sleep tracking team and the Beats team over the noise level in the test house, but we gave the sleepers some AirPods with noise cancellation, which should resolve the issue. Oh, and the Pope has expressed interest in trying the AI Siri pin. He loves his Apple Watch, and apparently His Holiness would like a screen-free way to brush up on his White Sox trivia in his downtime. Sentiment among beta testers on the smart glasses is a tad low — “Creepy as F—” tends to come up a lot in feedback. The team remains confident and has some anti-creep modifications planned. At least Meta is giving us a pretty low hurdle to clear, right? This might be a segment to pay attention to after you’re settled in. There are growing concerns in how we can maintain our stance on privacy while putting cameras on people’s ears and in their glasses. Upcoming Key Activities Just a reminder of some upcoming events: The team is gathering tomorrow night for drinks celebrating Phil’s not-quite-retirement. Tim’s goodbye drinks thing is tonight, and as a parting gift, he wants to review last quarter’s production numbers, for old time’s sake. He really does have a different idea of “fun,” doesn’t he? He’ll be heading to DC immediately after; President Trump has requested his help troubleshooting an issue with his iPad. Also, you’ll find Kate’s retirement party on your calendar. And Jennifer’s retirement party. That’s a lot of exits, huh? At least Craig still insists he isn’t going anywhere. We’re keeping a close eye on him anyway. Of course, there’s your big debut as CEO coming up next week. Rehearsals have looked great — you’ve really been studying the Cook-ian “Good Morning!” bellow. Sure, investors will be looking for any sign of weakness. And a big price hike just as we’re introducing a new boss isn’t great timing. There’s a lot hinging on this keynote, you could say. If there’s any way we can help make your first day better, don’t hesitate. Just relax and remember you’re running the world’s most profitable company in a time of political uncertainty, a historic supply chain crisis, unprecedented governmental scrutiny, and top executive shuffling. No pressure, Big J! You got this. Time to surprise and shine!

articles.title: Poco’s F9 Ultra pairs an ultra-bright display with a glowing Bose subwoofer
articles.summary: The cheaper F9 Pro packs the same screen, but simpler stereo speakers.﻿
articles.body: Xiaomi spinoff brand Poco has partnered with Bose for the second year in a row for its flagship F9 Pro and Ultra phones. The F9 phones double down on amped up audio, with a light-up subwoofer built into the Ultra, along with extremely bright displays, enormous batteries, and what should be Poco’s best cameras yet. The F9 Ultra sees the return of the Bose-branded 2.1 sound system introduced on last year’s F8 Ultra. Poco has only slightly tweaked the hardware, upgrading each of the two main speakers while using the same subwoofer as before, but has changed the structure of the subwoofer mount to include a small LED ring around it. It’s only white, with no choice of color, but can be used for call and notification lights as well as rhythmic lighting during gaming or music, unlike the extremely limited HiLight feature in the new Pixel 11 phones. [Image: The subwoofer light is subtle unless you catch it at the right angle. This must be the loudest phone I’ve ever tested, but quality is also genuinely pretty impressive considering the size of the speaker involved. This won’t match the quality of a good Bluetooth speaker, but it’s good enough that I’d happily rely on this for playing music in a hotel room, and it’s a definite upgrade for audio while gaming or watching TV. There are a couple of audio profiles designed by Bose, plus a full customizable EQ. New to the F9 Ultra is support for Bose’s game audio engine, which can do things like accentuate the sound of enemy footsteps in an FPS. The 6.9-inch OLED display is the other key selling point here, and it also has a gaming element. For starters, it’s extremely bright, with what Poco says is a peak brightness of 10,000 nits. But the 185Hz refresh rate is also impressive, even if Poco says you’ll only hit that top speed during compatible games, of which there’ll be more than 20 at launch, including Clash of Clans and GTA: Liberty City Stories. Beyond that, the F9 Ultra has a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip, up to 16GB RAM and 1TB storage, and a capacious 8,050mAh silicon-carbon battery with 100W charging. The cameras sound solid too: a 200-megapixel main camera, 50-megapixel 5x periscope, and 50-megapixel ultrawide. Poco tends to prioritize performance over photography, but it still has Xiaomi’s excellent image processing running the show, so I’d expect good results from this. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The Ultra is joined by the F9 Pro, a similar phone that’s just a little stripped back. The Bose stereo speakers lack both the subwoofer and the notification LED, the 6.59-inch display is a little smaller but just as bright and fast, the 6,330mAh battery is smaller, and the telephoto and ultrawide cameras are worse. Interestingly, it’s powered by the 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series, a binned version of the chip with very slightly reduced performance. The F9 Ultra starts from a flagship-level €1,099.90 (about $1,275), though is launching at a much lower early bird price of €829.90 ($960). As for the Pro, it’s €899.90 ($1,040), with a €739.90 ($860) initial offer. Both phones will get four years of OS updates and six years of security support. Photography by Dominic Preston / The Verge

articles.title: Roku’s first OLED TVs undercut the midrange competition
articles.summary: Roku comes in cheaper than Sony, LG, or Samsung with an intriguing OLED option.
articles.body: Just a few weeks ago the only midrange OLED options available were from LG and Samsung. But after Sony officially announced the Bravia 6 last week, Roku has now launched its first-ever OLED TV — the Roku Pro Series — which will be followed by the step-up Pro Series LX next month. The Roku Pro Series has a 120Hz panel, four HDMI 2.1 ports, and supports Dolby Vision and HDR10 Plus. It also has auto low latency mode, FreeSync Premium, and VRR for gaming. A backlit Roku remote is included, and a remote finder button on the TV helps locate it when misplaced. The Pro Series LX is about twice as bright as the regular Pro Series, supports 144Hz VRR, and has a polarizer to reduce reflections. And of course both TV series use the Roku operating system. The Pro Series is exclusive to Amazon for 2026, available now, and comes in 55- and 65-inch sizes starting at $999. The Pro Series LX will be available in October in 55 inches for $1,299 and 65 inches for $1,599.

articles.title: Get ready for a really busy month of smartphones
articles.summary: More than 20 smartphones are tipped to launch this month alone, starting with IFA, then the Apple event, and then loads more following Snapdragon Summit.
articles.body: We’re not even half a day into September, and two new smartphones have already launched: the Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra. We’re expecting more this week, as the IFA trade show kicks off in Berlin, before we get new iPhones a week after that. And that’s only the beginning of what promises to be an exceptionally busy month for smartphone launches. For the decade I’ve worked in the industry, tech journalists have always spoken in hushed tones about the dreaded “Techtember,” when just about every tech company on the planet seems to be in unspoken agreement that it’s time to launch new products in time for the holiday buying season. (It’s followed, in particularly packed years, by Techtober too). In the last few years, the pressure has lessened a little, the release calendar stretching out into neighboring months. But in 2026, Techtember is back with a vengeance, especially when it comes to phones. It always starts with IFA. Europe’s biggest tech trade show attracts over 200,000 visitors and global manufacturers from across tech. IFA doesn’t have as many phone launches as it did a decade ago, when the likes of Sony, Samsung, and LG would routinely launch flagships at the show, but there’s still plenty on the way this week. [Media: Tecno has teased a bezelless concept phone, which it says it’ll be bringing to the show. TCL usually brings an array of E Ink-esque Nxtpaper phones to show, so I’d hope to see some at its press conference. There’s even an outside chance of a whole new foldable: Xiaomi is attending IFA for the first time ever, just a week after it teased the upcoming Xiaomi 18 Fold and promised the phone a launch in early September. Its September 3rd press conference would certainly make sense for that. Then there’s Apple. The company won’t be at IFA, but it has already announced a September 9th event, where we expect it to launch new iPhones. Rumor has it that it’s splitting its launch up in an act of solidarity with overworked phone reviewers (I wish), delaying the regular iPhone 18 to next spring and sticking to the Pros this month. Still, the long-awaited arrival of the first foldable iPhone should be enough to keep us busy. But that’s far from all that’s coming. Android Headlines reckons at least 20 phones will launch this month, and that might be a conservative estimate. Huawei will launch its latest trifold, the Mate XT 2, in China on September 7th, and perhaps the Mate 90 lineup too. Xiaomi will follow up the 18 Fold with the 18 Pro lineup later in the month. Vivo has confirmed its flagship X500 series will also arrive in September, and Honor has done the same for its Magic 9 flagships. Oppo’s Find X10 line has been heavily tipped to arrive in September too, though thankfully some suggest it might slip to the following month. Even OnePlus is expected to get in on the action: its OnePlus 16 rumored to release in September too — though not in the US or Europe. Why the sudden glut? I blame Qualcomm. It used to launch its flagship Snapdragon chips in December, but that launch date has steadily moved forward, in part to give manufacturers time to ship new products ahead of lucrative holiday sales seasons, both in China and abroad. So this year it’s holding its annual Snapdragon Summit from September 22nd to 24th, when it’s likely to reveal the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. Promptly after that, we can expect a rush of Android manufacturers announcing phones powered by the new silicon. With RAMageddon in full swing, the jury’s still out on how appealing these launches will be. Outside of Samsung’s fun Galaxy Z Fold 8, a lot of this year’s biggest phones have been rehashes of 2025 models with a price hike and a chipset bump — and occasionally not even that. At least we’ll have more foldables to be excited about, and hopefully a couple of manufacturers have another surprise or two in store. A month chock-full of phones, that I can do. But if we’re about to get a Techtember full of iterative updates that cost more, without delivering anything special? Wake me up when it’s Techtober.

articles.title: Sonos introduces new headphones, soundbar, and software in its biggest announcement in years
articles.summary: After two years of turmoil, Sonos attempts a triumphant return.
articles.body: At an event in New York City, Sonos announced two new audio products — the Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar and Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, details of which were found in an FCC filing in early August — and a major update to its audio operating system dubbed Sonos 27. It’s the biggest single Sonos announcement since 2024, when a new app rollout upset its customers and sent it into damage control mode. Software changes are core to Sonos’ announcements, with the company leaning heavily into AI integration with Sonos 27. This includes the company’s own Sonos 27voice assistant that it built in-house for music and system control. It’s coming as an early access, opt-in feature this fall. There’s also Sonos 27mcp, which gives the ability to connect any existing AI models such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini — although for some reason Google Assistant is still not natively supported. Sonos 27mcp launches in early access on September 8th. In addition, users will be able to create up to 10 of their own agents through Sonos 27 to run, with whichever model they choose. These custom agents can be given different voices and roles. Brandon Holley, senior director of product development, gave examples of having a moody detective give you the morning news or a motivational coach whisper motivational aspirations when you wake up. Custom agents won’t be available until sometime in 2027. Both Sonos 27mcp and the custom agents seem to expand the customization and control of a Sonos system beyond what the app and Sonos 27voice is capable of. [Image: Features like a new 8-band EQ for the Sonos Ace Ultra have been added to the app. All products compatible with the current Sonos app can be controlled with Sonos 27mcp, and everything with a microphone works with Sonos 27voice. When the Sonos custom agents are available, they’ll work everywhere Sonos 27voice is enabled. There are two new features being added to Sonos Fabric, which is the name given to its whole-home connected system. The wireless Play and Move 2 portable speakers can be used as surround sound speakers in a home theater system. Once in place, the speakers will automatically configure to their new positions and roles as surround speakers without needing to initiate setup in the Sonos app. It’s not possible to use this feature with a single Play or Move 2. Compatible Sonos headphones will now be included in a Sonos home system and support moving sound between speakers and headphones — the system senses the closest speaker and will pass the audio from it to the headphones. Headphone linking, as Sonos calls it, will roll out as an early access feature on September 29th. Sonos hints that this is just the beginning of added features, but no further details about possible future options were given. Improvements continue to come to the app, as well, again with feedback from the community, including the Sonos subreddit. Home, system, and search tabs will be added across the bottom of the screen, and a room sort option can be pinned to the top for easier access to a customizable list. There’s a cool feature that calls back to physical audio components: a virtual volume knob, you control with two fingers like you would in the real world. It’s not a major quality of life improvement, but it’s something that adds character and fun, and something I’ll probably use regularly. The new navigation, room sorts, and virtual volume knob starts rolling out on September 8 (although the volume knob will only launch on iOS at that time). Lockscreen controls for volume and play/pause are also returning to the app, and started rolling out on August 17th. System health views to help troubleshoot issues and presets will roll out at some point later this fall. It’s not just software announcements, though, as Sonos has two new products coming — the long-rumored Ace Ultra headphones and Beam Ultra soundbar. [Image: If the Ace Ultra add to what was already great about the Ace, they could compete with Sony and Apple. The Sonos Ace Ultra are what the original Sonos Ace should have been from the beginning — an integrated part of the Sonos ecosystem. They are built upon Sonos’ Headphone Engine 2, which allows them to use the headphone linking feature rolling out at the same time as the headphones release on September 29th. A button on the headphones allows audio to be passed between a speaker and the headphones. No phone is necessary if it’s out of reach. They look very similar to the Ace, with what appears to be slightly different button placement on the left ear cup. The Ace Ultra are also a little bigger, with a little more space in the ear cup, and 10 grams heavier. They have newly custom-designed 40mm drivers and 10 microphones for noise control (two more than the Ace) which Sonos claims makes their ANC twice as effective at noise cancellation than the Ace with “the frequencies that really matter,” as Brandon Holley told me. Those frequencies happen to be 65Hz (the general frequency of an HVAC) where the Sonos Ace Ultra are 2.2 times more effective, and 120Hz — the airplane drone range — where they’re 1.8 times better. No information is provided for performance with the chatter you might encounter at the coffee shop, for example. An adaptive EQ adjusts the sound, compensating for any air leaks in the headphones’ fit due to glasses, jewelry, or hair. It includes both a 3-band and 8-band EQ to customize the sound for your taste. In addition to SBC and AAC codecs, the Ace Ultra supports aptX Adaptive Lossless over Bluetooth, and 16-bit/48kHz high resolution when connected with USB-C. Battery life has improved by five hours, with the Sonos Ace Ultra offering up to 35 hours of listening with ANC on. A fast charge of three minutes gets an additional three hours of listening time. Instead of just black and white, the Ace Ultra are also available in a muted blue agave and beige sand color. The headphones release on September 29th for $449. [Image: The Beam Ultra adds up-firing speakers to its compact size, making it a true Atmos soundbar. The Beam Ultra is a completely redesigned 7.1.2 compact soundbar (as opposed to the 5.0 configuration of its predecessor), including two up-firing drivers to support Dolby Atmos spatial audio. The center channel mid-tweeter features a new waveguide, mechanic and acoustic design, and DSP, which includes four levels of AI speech enhancement for clarity. While the Beam Ultra still has a compact design, to accommodate the additional speakers it is just under four inches longer than the Beam Gen 2. It comes in a black or white matte finish, and will be available for purchase on September 29th for $699. With the headphones’ deeper integration into the Sonos ecosystem and the addition of up-firing drivers to the Beam Ultra, it looks like Sonos has made some great improvements to already solid products. But I won’t know for sure until I can dig into them for reviews. The app updates — particularly the AI integration — I’m a bit more cautious about. But Sonos is making the right move by rolling out the updates over time, allowing its users to opt in to early access instead of dumping it on everyone at once. This more measured approach could be what wins back the masses.

articles.title: Waymo kicks off public rides in Tampa, Denver, and San Diego.

articles.title: GOP hard-liners threaten rebellion over stopgap funding bill
articles.summary: A small group of conservatives in the House of Representatives is threatening to vote against a procedural rule and stymie much of the GOP agenda for the week to protest a Senate-passed government funding bill the lower chamber is set to take up Tuesday. The hard-liners likely can’t block the funding bill itself, which is…
articles.body:
A small group of conservatives in the House of Representatives is threatening to vote against a procedural rule and stymie much of the GOP agenda for the week to protest a Senate-passed government funding bill the lower chamber is set to take up Tuesday.

The hard-liners likely can’t block the funding bill itself, which is known as a continuing resolution (CR) and would keep the government open through Dec. 11. The CR will come to the floor “under suspension,” meaning it doesn’t require a rule vote but will need a two-thirds majority to pass.

But the detractors could effectively freeze the floor and stall Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) from getting anything else done on the floor by tanking the rule, which would prevent other bills leadership wants passed from coming up for a vote.

Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) told reporters Monday night he’s voting no on the rule in an attempt to freeze the floor from other legislation.

He said he takes issue with several provisions in the Senate-passed CR, including its short-term delay on a ban on certain hemp products. He wants a “clean” continuing resolution or a chance to add his own priorities, like reupping a ban on federal funds going to Planned Parenthood that lapsed in the summer.

“All of this could’ve been handled either by putting it in the rule and allowing some amendments or just doing a clean CR, they didn’t do that,” Roy said of the Senate. “So I’ve got major problems with that.”

Roy sent a letter Monday to Reps. Tom Cole (R-Okla.) and Jodey Arrington (R-Texas), who chair the relevant committees on the CR, laying out his concerns.

Rep. Andy Harris (R-Md.), chair of the House Freedom Caucus, also indicated he was against the rule as of Tuesday morning, citing concerns about the hemp ban delay. Rep. Pete Sessions (R-Texas), who is not usually one to defy leadership, also said Tuesday he would vote no.

Other Republicans have also voiced concerns about a provision in the Senate-passed CR that would delay a rule giving White House political appointees greater authority over whether to disburse federal grants.

Johnson can afford to lose just three Republicans on the rule vote, assuming every member is present and voting. But campaign season is in full swing, and dozens of lawmakers missed Monday night’s vote, which means attendance issues could create another complication.

Cole told reporters Tuesday morning he had not yet received Roy’s letter and said while he is “sympathetic” with Harris’s concerns about the hemp ban, it’s not worth risking a government shutdown before the midterm elections by changing or failing to pass the CR.

“This should not have been on here, CR should not be controversial, so I’m sympathetic with that,” Cole said.

He criticized the use of the rule as leverage, since traditionally, members are expected to vote with their party on the rule, regardless of how they plan to vote on the legislation itself.

“A lot of this is we’ve got a group that wants to leverage the procedural votes to extract things that the majority of us probably don’t want to do. I find that disappointing,” Cole said. “I mean, if you’re going to be a member of the Republican conference, you ought to be able to vote for the rule. It’s just that simple, and you shouldn’t use it to leverage things against your own team. You want to vote against the bill? That’s perfectly fine, and that’s true in any bill. Your final vote on the bill is up to you, but blackmailing your colleagues is not the way to build an effective team.”

Cole said he still expected solid support for the CR because he also anticipated that some Democrats would vote for it.

Others in the Freedom Caucus indicated they would support the rule. Rep. Ben Cline (R-Va.) told The Hill on Tuesday he generally supports rules and would vote for this one. Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.) said he was “leaning toward voting for it” but would talk more with his colleagues first.

articles.title: GoPro to be acquired for $285M, will remain a public company | TechCrunch
articles.summary: GoPro is merging with a company that builds AI infrastructure, and will continue supporting existing consumer products.
articles.body:
After years of financial struggles, action camera pioneer GoPro is being acquired for $285 million.

A company called “Starman Optical” has agreed to merge with GoPro. The deal involves Starman Optical paying GoPro shareholders $1.14 per share, and leaving those shareholders with about 10% of the newly combined company. The deal, expected to close by the end of this year, will wipe away GoPro’s outstanding debt of $92 million.

The merger, announced Tuesday morning, comes a few months after GoPro revealed it was considering pivoting from building cameras to becoming a defense tech company. A day or so ago, YouTuber Markiplier revealed he had amassed an 8.5% stake in GoPro.

That appears to still be on the cards, as the company said the merger will “maximize the value of GoPro’s IP and growth potential in consumer, commercial and defense markets by recapitalizing the company, strengthening its balance sheet, investing in growth and onshoring the manufacturing of products for strategic markets.”

GoPro will also “fully support” its existing consumer products while “investing in growth and a broader, diversified product roadmap.”

It’s not exactly clear what all that means, and Starman Optical doesn’t have a significant track record to judge its performance.

The company bills itself as an “optical-photonics company focused on the development and domestic manufacturing of optical transceivers and related photonics technologies through its Starman New Photonics business.” Both Starman Optical and Starman New Photonics are part of Starman Holdings, which owns consumer tech brands like Incase, Incipio and Griffin.

Starman Optical was only incorporated in Delaware on August 31, while Starman New Photonics appears to have been created in 2025, and is building a manufacturing facility in New Jersey .

“Advanced optics and imaging are essential to AI, national security, and the broader economy, yet much of the critical hardware supporting these technologies continues to be manufactured overseas,” Charles Tebele, the CEO of Starman Holdings, said in a statement. “The combination of GoPro’s world-class optical expertise and intellectual property with Starman’s advanced transceiver capabilities and U.S. manufacturing platform creates a unique opportunity. Together, we intend to bring production of these critical components back to the United States.”

GoPro went public in 2014, when its action cameras were selling millions of units per year. In the decade since, the company tried branching into new categories like drones and 360-degree cameras, but it didn’t find much luck with either. GoPro then refocused on high-performing versions of its action cameras, and kept them targeted at pros, prosumers and athletes, but it had to conduct multiple rounds of layoffs as it narrowed the business.

In June, GoPro warned shareholders that it may go out of business without new funding . The following month, founder and CEO Nick Woodman said he was putting $20 million into the business to keep things going.

“We expect this merger to enable GoPro to grow across consumer, commercial and defense markets as a leading American imaging and optical solutions company, addressing important areas of national security related to cameras, optics and AI infrastructure. We’re excited to combine with the Starman team to capitalize on this opportunity and play an important role in America’s future,” Woodman said in a statement.

articles.title: Sony’s new party speakers have more bass, more LEDs, and more connectivity
articles.summary: Sony is expanding its ULT Power Sound party speaker line with three new tower-style models featuring improved lighting and deeper bass.
articles.body: Sony announced three new tower-style party speakers that will now be the largest options in its ULT Power Sound lineup. The new ULT Tower Max, ULT Tower 7, and ULT Tower 5 all feature expanded connectivity including USB-C, RCA, and XLR ports for connecting to audio gear using physical cables. The new models also come with improved lighting using up to 100 LEDs to provide visual feedback for functions like battery life and Bluetooth syncing in addition to creating an animated light show synced to what you’re listening to. [Image: All three of Sony’s new ULT Power Sound speakers come with RCA, USB-C, XLR ports on the back for connecting to audio sources (or other speakers) with cables. The largest of the new ULT Power Sound speakers is the $1,499.99, 121-pound Tower Max that looks big enough to double as a coffee table. Four tweeters, two midrange drivers, and three 280mm woofers work together to deliver what Sony describes as “the most powerful bass yet” in its ULT Power Sound collection. [Image: The 50-pound Tower 7 is less than half the weight of the Tower Max but still includes wheels on the bottom for easier maneuverability. All three of the new speakers feature four redesigned handles to improve portability while the Tower Max and Tower 7 also feature wider wheels for better maneuverability. For the first time users can also tweak the EQ settings for the speakers’ default sound profiles including ULT1 and ULT2 that maximize bass or the Flat mode that more accurately reproduces a song’s original mix with less of a chest-thumping experience. [Image: Although it’s the smallest of the three new speakers, the 29-pound ULT Tower 5 is by no means a small wireless speaker. The 50-pound, $649.99 Tower 7 features a single 280mm woofer paired with two midrange drivers and four tweeters that can run for up to 30 hours on a built-in rechargeable battery with the LED lighting turned off. The smallest of the three new models is the 29-pound, $449.99 Tower 5 that offers up to 20 hours of battery-powered playback through a 230mm woofer, two midrange drivers, and a pair of tweeters. It also has the same IPX4 water-resistance as the Tower 7, but only when the speakers are used standing vertically. The Tower Max is only “splash proof” on its top panel so you’ll want to stick to using it indoors.

articles.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra hits its lowest price since launch
articles.summary: Featuring bonus deals on the Remarkable Paper Pro Move, Insta360 X5, and The Mandalorian and Grogu on 4K Blu-Ray.
articles.body: If you missed the release promotions for the recent round of Samsung Galaxy phones, you’re in luck. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is $300 off at Best Buy, the best deal we’ve seen since the phone launched last month. The phone impressed us with its rear triple camera setup, excellent battery life, and slim, refined design, but the price held it back from true greatness. That’s helped by the discount, which brings the price down to $1,799.99 for the 256GB model. [Product: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra | The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra received a number of improvements over the previous generation’s Z Fold 7, including brighter interior and exterior screens, sharper cameras, and faster charging. The improved hinge design should be more durable, although it didn’t quite hold up to JerryRigEverything’s rigorous testing, and the IP48 water and dust resistance is lower than other folding phones like the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. The larger battery, up to 5,000mAh from the Z Fold 7’s 4,400mAh, helps the device last a full day on a single charge. Read our Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra review. Other deals to consider * The Remarkable Paper Pro Move note-taking tablet is on sale for $469 at Best Buy, $100 off its usual price. This 7.3-inch tablet can run for up to two weeks on a single charge, with a multi-color screen for highlighting important text, calling attention to specific notes, or just making your doodles more engaging. * Amazon and Insta360 have the Insta360 X5 discounted to $464.99, an $85 discount from the typical price. The X5 captures video at 120fps in 4K, and surprised us with its excellent image quality, particularly in low light. There are still some improvements to be made, particularly around software and weight, but the discount makes it a great choice for a first 360-degree camera. Read our review. * If you’re like me and missed The Mandalorian and Grogu movie in theaters, the 4K Blu-Ray is $24.77 at Amazon, about five dollars lower than its usual price. While my colleague Charles Pulliam-Moore felt the story might have been better told as another season of the show, as an avid Star Wars fan, I would still like to see the baby. Read our review.
